# Write: Your own study

## Create your report

```bash
Rscript scripts/R/create_report.R my-study
```

Open `reports/my-study-report.qmd`. The helper creates a separate Quarto project inside ignored `reports/` and preserves existing writing. The tracked starter lives in `templates/report.qmd`. Follow [Write the report](../../02-write-the-report.qmd) for the shared structure.

## Turn the checks into evidence

Use only your study's values and documented condition meanings. Include the source, independent biological replicate counts, pairing where applicable, final model/contrast and any code adaptation. Do not transfer numerical results or sample IDs from the worked examples.

Report the input gene count, retained gene count, available adjusted p-values and the decision threshold separately. Include a checked sample summary and normalized-count example. Explain unresolved design or quality limits and identify one justified follow-up. A result with no genes meeting the threshold is still a result.

## Render and review

From the main project folder:

```bash
cd reports
quarto render my-study-report.qmd
cd ..
```

Read `reports/my-study-report.html`. The starter links all six figures in `../results/my-study/figures/` and embeds them in the rendered HTML. Confirm they display, remove bracketed starter text and trace every number to a table or calculation. Existing older reports are not rewritten automatically; update their image paths and rendering configuration as needed.

**Your task:** identify one statement supported by an independent calculation, one by the fitted model, and one describing a limitation. State how AI helped and what you checked yourself.

Keep generated reports and HTML in ignored `reports/`, separate from book chapters. Inspect content for private data before sharing.
